blocks.text: Decoplex is an aesthetic that was mostly found in movie theaters in the 1990s and 2000s. It is the third wave of Art Deco motifs after Disco Deco and Deco-Luxe, but is less focused on luxury and more restrained and more inspired by the 1930s-40s golden age of Hollywood, WPA murals, and early air travel.

The visuals of the aesthetic evokes a theatrical, playful and cinematic feeling like a retro-futuristic dream of the mid-20th century portrayed through a 1990s lens. The color palette consists of vibrant neons, rich jewel tones, or contrasting cool or warm tones mixed with chrome and black accents. Motifs include swoops, sunbursts, arches, bold streamlined curves, and geometric lines.
Movie Multiplexes: Massive neon-lit geometric patterned carpets, concession stands, and towering designed entryways (such as AMC theater builds and classic 1990s Regal).
Materiality: Heavily utilizes chromium edging, glass brick windows, brushed steel, vitrolite glass, and custom neon light tracking or stylized terrazzo.
Bold Typography: Thick, center-extruded geometric fonts incorporating polished metallic, prominent drop shadows or neon edging.
Transit & Public Works: Modernized zigzag architecture in early 1990s metro stations (such as parts of the Los Angeles Metro Rail).
Aerodynamic Diners: The 90s revival of classic checkerboard patterns, chromium-edged booths, and streamlined, curved silver diners.
